A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MultiVox benchmark. Their text, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison. V1 ends with references; v2 adds appendices A–G, which were also inspected.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations in Table 2, error and confounder analyses, and a 100-query human-versus-synthetic speech-quality study in Section 3.4.

after.justification: V2 reports revised model evaluations and diagnostic analyses, retains the speech-quality study, and adds a 300-item human-versus-LLM judge validation in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The benchmark retains its joint speech/vision task design and confounder pairs with identical text and visuals but altered speech properties. V2 introduces no new proposed model, training objective, or inference algorithm.

E1.justification: Coverage remains 1,000 English spoken queries paired with images or videos across acoustic scene understanding, paralanguage, and speaker profiling. Appendix B elaborates existing categories and identifies an audio source; it does not establish added task coverage. The judge-validation sample comes from the existing benchmark.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes the Lyra and Gemini 2.0 Flash rows and adds VideoLlama2, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and a Qwen 2.5 Omni COT variant. These changes substantially revise the reported comparison set, particularly its proprietary-model coverage. The CosyVoice and ElevenLabs comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds a blind 300-item judge-validation protocol using three expert raters and one GPT-4.1-mini judgment per item, plus a Qwen COT evaluation condition. The main VG, SG, and CA metrics remain. Newly documented noise mixing and judge details do not establish that settings changed for existing runs.

E4.justification: Section 5 substantially revises the failure analyses around Gemini 2.5 Pro and Qwen, including speaker attributes, background sounds, emotion, and confounder responses. Appendix D adds an empirical test of judge reliability, while Table 2 adds a COT comparison. Appendix E expands documentation of the existing speech-quality study rather than introducing another study.

E5.justification: Appendices C–D newly report at least 90% agreement on 50 pilot annotations, human–human Cohen's kappa of 0.82, human–LLM kappa of 0.78, and ratings within one point in 92% of cases. V1 lacks these agreement estimates. Neither version reports uncertainty across repeated model runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces many reported scores for retained models: Qwen's average CA changes from 2.91 to 3.08 and phi4's from 2.79 to 2.44. New results include Gemini 2.5 Pro at 3.56 and Qwen COT at 3.19. Sections 5.1–5.3 and Figures 4–5 revise diagnostic findings, and the appendices add agreement and distribution results. These are reported revisions and additions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The conceptual benchmark definitions remain, and the new agreement statistics do not introduce mathematical derivations or formal properties.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claim that current models struggle to current open-source models, and the stated evaluation coverage increases from nine to ten models. The introduction and conclusion retain the benchmark's novelty, confounder-pair contribution, and central speech-grounding bottleneck claim.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the interpretation of proprietary/open-source parity with a proprietary-model advantage. It also distinguishes Gemini's successful perception of speaker attributes from failure to incorporate them into final responses, and adds a limitation concerning spoken grounding instructions. The English-only and output-speech-quality limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New appendices document MS-Noise mixing at -2 dB, annotation preparation, the judge model and scoring rubric, actor recruitment and IRB approval, A6000 hardware, inference times, and implementation/API usage. V2 also discloses synthetic children's voices and replaces the example-site link with a GitHub link. Media accounting changes from 560 images/440 videos to 206 unique images/287 unique videos, without reconciling the counting units.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Video-LLaMA by Zhang et al. and the work by Nachmani et al., and removes the DailyTalk reference by Lee et al. The Lyra related-work citation remains despite removal of its evaluated row. The broader positioning against existing benchmarks is largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 edits the title and author header, replaces many OVA references with OLM terminology, rewrites portions of the results discussion, and adds organized appendices. The main section order and most benchmark-design and related-work prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands and reorders model rows. Figures 4–5 are redrawn with revised labels, styling, and plotted results, while new Figures 6–7 display category distributions. The existing benchmark illustrations, table organization, and overall two-column layout remain substantially similar.

improvement.justification: The new human–judge validation and explicit rubric provide support missing from v1's tentative judge description, while implementation details make the benchmark more auditable. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Section 4 still names Gemini 2.0 despite Table 2 reporting Gemini 2.5 models, and blanket human-recording claims conflict with the newly disclosed synthetic children's voices. The revision improves evidential support and documentation, but does not resolve these consistency problems.
